sentences.text:
This revision is filed by the accused/revision petitioner under Section 397 r/w 401 of Cr.P.C.,
challenging the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Principal Civil Judge &
J.M.F.C., Karkal, in C.C.No.48/2010, dated 24.07.2013 and confirmed by the Principal Sessions Judge, Udupi, in Crl.A.No.83/2013 vide judgment dated 24.04.2015.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred with the original ranks occupied by them before the trial Court.

3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are as under:
It is the case of the prosecution that on 04.12.2009 at 5.45 p.m., the accused being the driver of Vishal Company bus bearing No.KA20/A-9659 drove the same on Hebri-Karkala Tar Road from Hebri side towards Karkarla side in a rash and negligent manner and in front of Mudrady Government Higher Primary School he dashed NC: 2023:KHC:33522 against a motor bike bearing No.KA19/L-7000 driven by the deceased Govinda Bhat which was coming from Karkala side and moving towards Hebri and as a result, the rider of the bike Govinda Bhat sustained a grievous injuries and subsequently, he succumbed because of the injuries in KMC hospital,
Manipal on 08.11.2009 at 7.45 p.m., without responding to the treatment.

Initially,
the complaint was lodged for the offence punishable under Sections 279 & 338 of IPC and subsequently, the charge sheet has been submitted for the offence punishable under Sections 279 & 304A of IPC.

4. After submission of the charge sheet, as there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused, the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offence and issued process against the accused.
The accused has appeared through his counsel and was enlarged on bail.

He was also provided with prosecution papers as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
NC: 2023:KHC:33522 5.
The plea under Sections 279 & 304A of IPC is framed against the accused and same is read over and explained to the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Thereafter, the prosecution has examined in all five witnesses as PW1 to PW5 and also placed reliance on nine documents marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.

After conclusion of the evidence of the prosecution, the statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C., is recorded to enable the accused to explain the incriminating evidence appearing against him in the case of the prosecution.
The case of accused is of total denial.
The accused has also not lead any oral or documentary evidence in support of his defence.

6. After having heard the arguments and after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the learned Magistrate has convicted the accused for the offence punishable under Sections 279 & 304A Sri.

Arthar David vs The State on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182335163/
2 of IPC.
Being aggrieved by this judgment of conviction and order of sentence, the accused has approached the Principal Sessions Judge, Udupi, in Crl.A.No.83/2013.

7. The learned Sessions Judge after re- appreciating the oral and documentary evidence has dismissed the appeal by confirming the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the learned Magistrate.
Being aggrieved by these concurrent findings, the accused is before this Court by way of this revision.
8. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned HCGP for State.
Perused the records.

9. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner would contend that the evidence on record clearly discloses that PW1 is not an eyewitness and he rushed to the spot after the accident and hence, he cannot be NC: 2023:KHC:33522 considered to be a competent witness to depose regarding rash &
negligent act.

He would also contend that at the accident spot, there are two bus stops opposite to each other and hence, it is the deceased who in a process of overtaking the vehicle, caused the accident and there is no actionable negligence on the part of the accused/revision petitioner.

Alternatively, he would also submit that the sentence of six months and one year for the offence punishable under Sections 279 & 304A of IPC respectively appears to be high and hence, he would contend that considering the age of the accused and the place of the accident, some leniency may be shown by reducing the sentence.
10.
Per contra, learned HCGP would contend that PW1 & PW2 are eyewitnesses to the accident and they have deposed as per the case of the prosecution.

He would also contend that accident, death,
involvement of the bus and two-wheeler and the accused being the driver of the offending vehicle have been admitted and hence it is for the accused to explain as to under what circumstances the NC: 2023:KHC:33522 accident has occurred.
But his 313 Cr.P.C. statement is silent.
He would further assert that the evidence of PW1 & PW2 coupled with the evidence of PW3 to PW5 is sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused.
He would further assert that both the Courts below have also imposed a reasonable sentence which does not call for interference.

11. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, now the following point would arise for my consideration:
"Whether the Judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by both the Courts below are perverse, arbitrary and erroneous so as to call for any interference by this Court?"
12.
It is the specific assertion of the prosecution that the accused was the driver of the offending bus bearing No.KA20/A-9569 which was involved in the accident dated 04.12.2009 occurred at 5.45 Sri.

Arthar David vs The State on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182335163/
3 p.m., in Mudrady Village in front of Mudrady Government Higher School on Hebri-Karkala main road.

The defence has not disputed the accident, involvement of the bus as well as NC:
2023:KHC:33522 accused being the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is also an admitted fact that the said bus hit a two-wheeler driven by deceased Govinda Bhat which was coming from the opposite direction.

The deceased suffered fatal injuries and he was admitted to KMC hospital,
Manipal and subsequently, he succumbed because of the accident injuries.
These aspects have been admitted.
13. The accused has simply disputed the rash and negligent driving on his part.
The complainant is examined as PW1 and his complaint is marked at Ex.P1.
The complaint itself is lodged on 05.12.2009 at about 12.00 in the noon though the accident has taken place on 04.12.2009 at 5.45 p.m.

It is also evident that immediately after the accident, police rushed to the spot, but the conduct of the Police Officials in this regard is highly objectionable as they did not choose to register the crime and they asked some other person to lodge a complaint.
This conduct of the Police discloses that they want to shoulder their responsibility.
At the same time, the accused having caused the accident, has not reported the accident to the nearest Police Station.
It is not the case that he has attended the injured also and it was the duty of the accused to immediately attend the injured and shift him to the hospital, but that was also not done.
It is also an offence under the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
But interestingly, the investigating officer has not prosecuted the accused for the said offence.

15. The complainant is examined as PW1 and in his evidence, he has deposed that on 04.12.2009, he was moving towards Mudrady market from his shop and at the time, the accused drove his bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed a two-wheeler coming from the opposite direction.
This witness was cross

- examined at length and it is elicited that he rushed to the spot after the accident,
but merely on the said admission it cannot be presumed that he is not an eyewitness.
PW2 is another eyewitness and he has also supported the case of the prosecution.
Further, the evidence of PW2 clearly discloses that when he rushed to the spot, PW1 was already present there.
Hence, the presence of PW1 is quite natural.
The evidence of PW1 & PW2 is consistent.
17. PW3 to PW5 are the investigating officers and PW2 is also a mahazar witness apart from being an eyewitness.
Admittedly, at the accident spot, the road is running from North to South.
Hebri is situated towards the North and the bus was moving from Hebri and it was moving towards the South.
The accident spot is not on the Eastern side of the road, but it is on the Western side of the road.
Admittedly, the motorbike rider was proceeding from Karkala towards Hebri and he was moving on the left side i.e., Western side of the road.

It is for the accused to explain as to why he Sri. Arthar David vs The State on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182335163/
4 compelled to drive his vehicle on the Northern side of the road.

sentences.text: But there is no explanation forthcoming in this regard.

The sketch of the scene of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:33522 offence produced at Ex.P3 clearly establishes that the accident in question is because of actionable negligence on the part of the accused, who was the driver of the offending bus.

18. Further, during the evidence, accused has set up a defence that the Padmambika Bus was moving from Karkala to Hebri at the time of the accident and the deceased in the process of overtaking the bus, hit the on coming offending bus driven by the accused, which has resulted in the accident.
But in 313 Cr.P.C. statement given by the accused no such defence was forthcoming.

Even if the defence of the accused is taken note of, then it is again for the accused to explain why he crossed the medial line towards right i.e., towards the Western side, as he was required to drive his bus in the eastern side.

The accused has not explained any of these aspects and as such, the evidence on record clearly establishes that the accident in question is because of actionable negligence on the part of the accused.
Both the Courts below have - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:33522 appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in proper perspective by elaborately discussing the evidence.
No perversity or illegality is found in the judgment of conviction so as to call for any interference by this Court.
Hence, the question of interfering with the judgment of conviction does not arise at all.

19. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner would contend that sentence of imprisonment for six months for offence punishable under Section 279 and one year for the offence punishable under Section 304A of IPC appears to be on the higher side.
Hence, he would submit that fine along with some compensation may be awarded by reducing the sentence of imprisonment.
The offence under Section 304A of IPC itself is causing death by reckless act.
When the accused is being convicted under Section 304A of IPC, there is no need for again sentencing him for the offence under Section 279 of IPC also.
The offence under Section 279 of IPC merges with larger offence under Section 304A of IPC.
As such, the question - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:33522 of imposing independent sentence for the offence punishable under Section 279 of IPC does not arise at all.
20 . The offence is said to have been taken on State highway i.e., Hebri-Karkala Main Road.

From the accident spot, at a distance of about 200 feet, there is a curve and this accident spot is on Hebri Road which joins Karkala and Bachadri Road and there was a Mudrady Circle wherein the deviation for Hebri takes place.
The accused is aged about 61 to 62 years as on today.
The matter is pending since 2010 and lot of water has flown in between.

Considering these aspects, in my considered Sri. Arthar David vs The State on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182335163/
5 opinion the sentence of imprisonment for a period of one year appears to be on higher side.

sentences.text: Considering the age of the accused/revision petitioner and place of accident, in my considered opinion, it is just and proper to impose a sentence of imprisonment for four months by enhancing the fine to Rs.10,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 304A of IPC, which will serve the purpose along with the default clause.
Considering these facts and circumstances, revision - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:33522 petition needs to be allowed in part so far as it relates to the sentence portion.
As such, the point under consideration is partly answered in the affirmative.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The revision petition is allowed in part so far as it relates to the sentence portion is concerned.

(ii) The judgment of conviction passed by the Principal Civil Judge & J.M.F.C.,
Karkal, in C.C.No.48/2010, dated 24.07.2013 and confirmed by the Principal Sessions Judge, Udupi, in Crl.A.No.83/2013 vide judgment dated 24.04.2015, stands confirmed.
(iii) However, the sentence imposed for the offence punishable under Section 279 of IPC, is set aside.

(iv) So far it relates to the offence under Section 304A of IPC, the accused is directed to undergo a simple imprisonment for a period of four months and is directed to pay Rs.10,000/- in default, he is required to undergo further imprisonment for a period of one month.
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:33522 Send back TCRs to the trial Court with a direction to secure the presence of the accused for serving the sentence and collection of arrears of fine, if any.
